source_refs.locator: PDF pp. 43–44 (printed pp. 44–45), Melekeok vulnerability assessment.

evidence.scenario: The 2013 assessment considers sea-level rise, storm surge and waves through 2100.
evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2013-09 reports: The assessment placed most coastal homes, tourist lodging and utility lines within 30 metres of Melekeok’s high-water mark, vulnerable to sea rise, waves and typhoons.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 44 (printed p. 45), Melekeok coastal wastewater-treatment plant assessment.

evidence.scenario: Projected sea-level rise and storm surge.
evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2013-09 reports: It identified the southern-coast wastewater plant as a low-lying mangrove-edge asset at risk of inundation, damage and sewage release.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 44 (printed p. 45), Ngardok Nature Reserve and water-supply assessment.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2013-09 reports: Ngardok Nature Reserve covers one-third of Melekeok and supplies its only drinking water; prolonged drought is identified as its greatest natural-system threat, alongside flood and erosion risks.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: PDF pp. 44–45 (printed pp. 45–46), Melekeok assessment outputs and implementation status.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2013-09 reports: Proposed outputs included resilient wastewater, watershed and water-supply systems plus a state adaptation plan; no project adaptation strategies had yet been implemented.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: The 2025 water policy identifies the Ngerikiil catchment in Airai as the primary supply area for Airai and Koror. Its population-coverage figures vary between passages, so the bank retains qualitative dependence rather than a precise current coverage share.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2025 reports: While Koror–Airai water quality is described as good, small rural Babeldaob plants often have high turbidity after heavy rain and sometimes detect E. coli or coliforms.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 2, executive summary; pp. 22–23, Iporu/Tobi site assessment and recommendations.

affected_groups: Palauan communities with cultural ties to Tobi
evidence.scenario: Projected inundation risk; no sea-level scenario is specified.
evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2021 reports: At Iporu on Tobi, surveyors found erosion had exposed archaeological remains; low-lying Tobi cultural sites (3–4 metres and below) were considered at risk of inundation.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: PDF pp. 24–27, Kayangel traditional-village assessment and recommendations.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2021 reports: The report describes 2012–13 typhoon-driven debris, saltwater inundation affecting Kayangel gardens and homes, and flooding again in April 2021 at the low-lying traditional-village sites.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: PDF pp. 33–34, Odalmelech monolith assessment in Melekeok State.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2021 reports: At the Melekeok coast, four stone monoliths had been undercut by erosion and were resting on the beach; the report recommends restoring and reinforcing the site and keeping a drainage culvert clear.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.
